cases.excerpt: We analyzed plasma concentrations of betaine, choline, cysteine, methionine, methylmalonic acid (MMA), vitamin B2, and vitamin B6 in 561 cases and 1,034 controls matched for age and recruitment date, nested within the population-based Northern Sweden Health and Disease Cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: The relative risks for a doubling in concentrations were 1.46 [95% confidence interval (95% CI), 1.04-2.05; P(trend) = 0.03] for choline, 1.11 (95% CI, 1.00-1.23; P(trend) = 0.04) for vitamin B2, and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.63-0.97; P(trend) = 0.03) for MMA. Concentrations of betaine, cysteine, methionine, and vitamin B6 were not associated with prostate cancer risk.

validated_results.title: Plasma phyto-oestrogens and prostate cancer in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within EPIC reporting relative risks for plasma genistein and subsequent prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest fifth of plasma genistein, adjusted for potential confounders

sample_size.excerpt: Concentrations of isoflavones genistein, daidzein and equol, and that of lignans enterolactone and enterodiol, were measured in plasma samples for 950 prostate cancer cases and 1042 matched control participants.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 950 + 1042 = 1992

cases.excerpt: Concentrations of isoflavones genistein, daidzein and equol, and that of lignans enterolactone and enterodiol, were measured in plasma samples for 950 prostate cancer cases and 1042 matched control participants.

effect_size.excerpt: After adjustment for potential confounders this RR was 0.74 (95% CI 0.54-1.00, P trend=0.05). No statistically significant associations were observed for circulating concentrations of daidzein, equol, enterolactone or enterodiol in relation to overall risk for prostate cancer.

validated_results.title: Serum lycopene and the risk of cancer: the Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor (KIHD) study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study of serum lycopene concentrations and incident prostate cancer among Finnish men.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest tertile of serum lycopene (no prostate-specific numeric estimate reported)

sample_size.excerpt: The study population consisted of 997 middle-aged Finnish men in the Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor (KIHD) cohort. During the mean follow-up time of 12.6 years, a total of 141 cancer cases appeared, of which 55 were prostate cancers.

cases.excerpt: During the mean follow-up time of 12.6 years, a total of 141 cancer cases appeared, of which 55 were prostate cancers.

comparison.excerpt: No association was observed between the lycopene concentrations and a prostate cancer risk.

design.excerpt: in the Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor (KIHD) cohort

timing.excerpt: During the mean follow-up time of 12.6 years

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The association between the serum concentrations of lycopene and the risk of cancer
